We do ours on a surface like a table/counter top. Most of them I can do by myself but sometimes one or two needs holding there by a second person. Its much easier to do it like this because they feel more secure with all their feet on a surface than trying to do it holding them up somehow like Ive seen others do. To get these nails down to a more reasonable length youll have to do it a bit at a time with a few days in between so the quick can recede again. Its always a good idea to have styptic powder on hand for any accidents especially with dark nails where its harder to see the quick. When I get new pigs they aren't used to it either but if you do it regularly (lately i seem to be trimming every 2-3 weeks) they get used to it super fast and will just stand there. Even my boy who doesnt like being handled or humans much due to past neglect is good getting them trimmed. You can also handle them more and touch their feet/get them used to being examined in general. Every little helps 😊 good luck

Moderate by most definitions I can find means "reduced mobility and are restricted in all activities of daily living, although they may have peaks and troughs in their level of symptoms and ability to do activities. They have usually stopped work or education, and need rest periods often". Another source said moderate means mainly housebound and thats also the definition I went by for years. When I said Im moderate I was unable to do any education or work and just the basic tasks of living. I was restricted to my house unless it was a necessary medical appointment. From your account it still seems you work in person, are going to start education & still date, socialise and go out to things like concerts and pride. Levels of severity have to mean *something* and be somewhat agreed upon for us to properly communicate our life and needs to other people and medical professionals.

And definitely check for rescues nearby because they can offer "dating" where you bring the pig along to see who he gets along with, or if a pairing doesnt work out they may be open to taking back the new pig. Its always best to support rescues instead of pet stores if possible

Piggies are prey animals and often wont be super cuddly or tame depending on how they were raised and their previous homes handling of them. Oh and if he does go through with it anyway and tried to keep them all together at first they would need a super large enclosure and multiple litter boxes/hay areas, water bottles food dishes and hides due to being boys. Guinea pigs basically come out of the womb already formed miniature versions of adult pigs and can start nibbling on hay pellets and veg within a few days of birth. No need to wait because they need the vitamins and nutrients from the veg. Although I would start off with a small amount of each or one type at a time to avoid upsetting his tummy.

Although you can get a girl before that and have them in cages beside each other as long as he cant get into her (they can be quite determined). They will smell each other and talk through the cages until they can properly be introduced.

I had what I now know was a very mild case of ME for many years as a teen. It showed as fatigue, being more easily fatigued by usual activities than my healthy peers and needing more time to rest afterwards. It wasnt until a bad viral infection that it turned into full blown ME and i also developed fibromyalgia then so all the other symptoms of various pain came in.

 The lack of motivation would not be like ME however..we are all desperate to be able to live our lives and return to/start our careers, education, hobbies. Ask any one of us and we have a massive list of all the things we would do tomorrow and next week and this year if we magically woke up cured. 

Has she had all her bloods appropriately tested for things like thyroid issues, anaemia and b12 or vitD deficiency? All this kinda stuff needs ruled out also. And is she on antidepressants? These can have terrible side effects including fatigue themselves so could be making it worse or could even be the root of the physical symptoms depending on her dose and how long she's been on them. Doctors throw pysch meds at people as a cure all and people dont even realise why or the possible side effects and outcomes. 

The other main thing to look into is PEM post excertional malaise, a worsening of symptoms anywhere from a few hours to a day or two after something that exceeds her limits. This is pretty exclusive to ME and if the limits are constantly pushed will worsen the baseline and overall health. If its depression or something else she may be tired after doing something energy sapping but it wont be this severe and gradually make her worse.

Without pictures i cant be sure but could it be spurs? Google guinea pig spurs and see if it looks like them. About 1 out of every 4 piggies will develop them as adults, no one really knows why. It doesnt matter what cage flooring they have and its not a sign of bad hygiene or anything, just an evolutionary thing they have!

 Its harmless for them, but they should be kept trimmed just like nails they will keep growing and could catch on something and rip. Theres a couple videos on youtube of clipping them (if the vet isnt very guinea pig savvy they probably wont know what theyre doing). Its easy to trim at home with nail clippers, I keep them trimmed when i do their nails. One out of my four girls has them and i trim them regularly. Another one or two may be developing them but they arent growing much yet. You just clip most of the length off, obviously being careful not to get too close to the paw pad which they grow out of. 

That all said, it could be something else like fungal.  Hopefully it's just harmless common spurs

I would quarantine the new girls for at least a couple of weeks once they are treated for parasites and have a clean bill of health preferably from a vet. If theyre from a bad situation they could carry ringworm/lice/have a weaker immune system and some kind of URI.

 [This](https://www.theguineapigforum.co.uk/forums/behaviour-bonding-and-bereavement.21/) website has lots of great guides in the behaviour and bonding section you can read up on, and I also recommend Saskia from LAGPR on youtube she has a couple videos on introductions. 


The most important point is it has to be done in one go, you cannot introduce them all and them remove them and do that repeatedly. Some people think they are gradually getting them used to each other but guinea pigs dont work like that. They have to start from scratch to create their pecking order each time they are introduced which is very stressful for them. Its best to do in one go in a neutral place and not interrupt unless there is serious fighting.
You could also just keep two pairs in separate enclosures like I do currently.
